scope: Proposition A.7 (Angular dispersion and bilinear estimates) of the manuscript “An unconditional first moment for cubic Gauss sums” (preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 023 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0af3e675f8a6a5b3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The estimates of Proposition 5.1 hold for βℓ, assuming (SW) for βℓ wherever it was required. For B > X.40, the stipulated structured class is exactly the angular prime-convolution class above. The conclusions of Propositions 7.1 and 7.2 consequently hold with the kernel multiplied by θℓ(ab) and with all their other hypotheses retained. The absolute small-B parameter γ is unchanged; other constants may depend on fixed ℓ.
